mechanism_narrative: The observed upward trend in RETAIL_REC over the past four weeks, from -16.3% to -11.6%, indicates a sustained recovery in consumer activity, which will continue to drive retail and recreation mobility higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If the mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the mean RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days (-14.75%), this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: As WORKPLACES mobility has now risen above -20% from baseline for two consecutive weeks (t-1w: -17.4%, t-0w: -16.4%), it signals a critical mass of return-to-office, which will boost weekday retail and recreation activity in the immediate future.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above -20% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If the mean RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks does not increase compared to the mean of the last two weeks (t-1w, t-0w), despite WORKPLACES remaining above -20%, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: The combined effect of a consistent decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility (from 9.6% to 5.9%) and a steady increase in TRANSIT usage (from -51.3% to -42.0%) suggests a shift away from home-bound activities and a greater reliance on public transport for outings, which will positively impact retail and recreation.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next four weeks, or if RESIDENTIAL mobility starts to rise again while TRANSIT declines, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: The recent high volatility in PARKS mobility, with a significant dip to -21.0% followed by a recovery to -7.1%, suggests that outdoor activities are still subject to external factors. If these factors stabilize, some activity may shift to indoor retail and recreation.
failure_condition: If PARKS mobility remains highly volatile or declines further, and RETAIL_REC does not increase in the next week, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent week-on-week increase in TRANSIT usage, from -51.3% to -42.0%, despite still being significantly below baseline, indicates a gradual return to pre-pandemic commuting and leisure travel patterns, which will directly support higher retail and recreation visits.
failure_condition: If TRANSIT mobility plateaus or declines over the next four weeks, and RETAIL_REC does not show a corresponding increase, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: As RESIDENTIAL mobility has now fallen below 6% from baseline (t-0w: 5.9%), it signifies a widespread shift in behavior where people are spending significantly less time at home, directly translating to more time spent in public spaces including retail and recreation venues.
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL mobility rises above 6% again or RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next two weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The concurrent rise in WORKPLACES mobility (from -28.9% to -16.4%) and stable-to-positive GROCERY_PHARM mobility (around 2-3%) suggests an increase in essential out-of-home activities, creating more opportunities for incidental retail and recreation visits during commutes or errands.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES mobility declines while GROCERY_PHARM also falls below baseline, and RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next four weeks, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: The broad upward trend across RETAIL_REC, TRANSIT, and WORKPLACES, coupled with a downward trend in RESIDENTIAL, strongly implies an ongoing easing of public health restrictions or a shift in public sentiment towards greater mobility, which will continue to boost retail and recreation.
failure_condition: If there is a reversal in the overall trend of increasing mobility across multiple categories (e.g., RETAIL_REC, TRANSIT, WORKPLACES decline, RESIDENTIAL rises) over the next four weeks, this hypothesis is falsified.
